transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, yeah, thank you. Well, honestly, what brings me in is just... my sleep has gotten really, really messed up lately. I work as a bookkeeping clerk, so I'm looking at spreadsheets and reconciling accounts all day, which means I really need my brain to be sharp, but right now it's just a disaster. 

I’ll get into bed at a normal time, like maybe 10:30 or 11:00, because I have to be at the office early, but I’ll just lay there. I end up staying up half the night with my mind just running and running about every little thing. Or, if I do actually manage to finally drift off, I'll wake up way, way too early—like 3:00 or 4:00 in the morning—and I just can't get back to sleep. I'll just stare at the ceiling feeling like I never even rested at all. 

And I've tried everything, you know? I tried drinking that chamomile sleepytime tea, I tried turning off my phone an hour before bed so I'm not looking at a screen, I tried reading a boring book... but nothing helps. It’s just so incredibly frustrating when you are physically exhausted but your mind just refuses to let you shut down, and it's making my days so hard to get through at work. I just keep staring at the numbers feeling like a zombie. So, yeah, that's really what's going on.
Do you find yourself feeling worried or anxious about things more often than not, even when there isn’t a specific reason to be?

I mean... no? Not really. It’s not like I’m sitting around biting my nails or feeling like something terrible is going to happen for no reason. When I said my mind is running and running at night, it’s not usually about bad things or, you know, impending doom. It’s more just... loud? 

Like, I’ll be laying there in the dark and suddenly I’m thinking about the grocery list, or this one cell on an Excel sheet that wouldn’t format right for me yesterday, or maybe a conversation I had with my neighbor three days ago about her cat. Just completely random stuff. So I wouldn't really call it anxiety or worry, because I don't feel scared or nervous about it. I just feel incredibly, incredibly annoyed. Because I know I need to sleep, and my brain is just going on and on about completely useless things that don't even matter in the grand scheme of things. 

And then during the day, I'm definitely not anxious either, I'm just so tired. I'm just dragging myself through the shift, practically drinking my weight in coffee just to keep my eyes open while I'm looking at the ledgers. So, yeah, I don't think I'm a worrier, really. Just... I don't know, frustrated that I can't just flip a switch and turn my brain off when I'm supposed to.
Have you been feeling down, sad, or hopeless most days lately, even before the sleep issues started?

Well... yeah. Honestly, yes. And it's funny you ask if it was before the sleep stuff started, because I was actually just thinking about that the other day. I was sitting at my kitchen island—which I love, by the way, I spent months saving up for this specific condo because it has this beautiful open-concept kitchen, and I was so, so proud when I finally closed on it—but I was just sitting there looking at it, and I felt absolutely nothing. Or, no, not nothing, but just this incredibly heavy, empty feeling in my chest. Like someone had poured lead in there.

And it’s been happening a lot lately, actually. I’ll wake up—well, if you can call it waking up when you barely slept—but I'll get out of bed and just feel this overwhelming sadness. It's so weird because I have a good job, I have my own place, I should be happy. But instead, I just sit there in my beautiful condo that I worked so hard for, and I just want to cry. And I do cry, sometimes. Just sitting there with my coffee, tears running down my face for absolutely no reason that I can pinpoint. 

It definitely started before the sleep got this bad, maybe a few weeks before? I remember I was at work, reconciling the end-of-month accounts for one of our bigger clients, and usually I get a little kick out of making all the numbers balance perfectly. It's satisfying, you know? But that day, I just stared at the screen and felt so completely hopeless. Like, what is the point of any of this? Why am I even doing this? And that heavy feeling just kind of settled over me and hasn't really left since. So, yeah, I guess I have been feeling pretty down. It's just exhausting, on top of not sleeping.
Have you noticed that you take less pleasure or interest in activities that you used to enjoy, or do things feel less rewarding than they used to?

Yeah... yeah, I definitely have. It's actually really sad when I think about it, because I used to have things that I genuinely looked forward to at the end of the week. Like, I used to go to this salsa dancing class every Thursday night. I started going maybe, I don't know, two years ago? A friend from high school dragged me to it originally because she didn't want to go alone, and she ended up quitting after a month, but I actually loved it. It was such a great way to shake off the stress from staring at spreadsheets all week, and the music was so upbeat, and I even bought these special shoes for it... but I just completely stopped going. I haven't been in weeks. The thought of getting dressed and driving over there and trying to follow the steps just feels like climbing Mount Everest. 

And it’s not just the big things that require leaving the house, either. It’s stuff right in my own apartment. I used to really like painting—not like I'm some amazing artist or anything, just watercolor stuff, mostly landscapes or little abstract designs. I actually have this nice little setup in the corner of my living room by the window where the light is good in the afternoon. But my paints are just... they're still sitting out on the table exactly where I left them weeks ago. The water cup is completely dried out, the brushes are just lying there gathering dust. And I walk past that table every single day, and I look at the paints, and I just feel absolutely nothing. It's the weirdest sensation, honestly. It's like I'm looking at someone else's hobbies, like those paints belong to a completely different person who used to live here. I don't even have the urge to pick up a brush. I just look at it and feel that same heavy emptiness, and then I just go sit on the couch and stare at the wall instead. So, yeah, I guess nothing really feels rewarding or fun anymore. It's just all so flat.
Would you say that you've completely lost interest or pleasure in almost all activities, even ones you used to really enjoy?

Well, yeah, I guess that’s exactly what I’m trying to say, you know? It’s just... it’s all of it. Almost everything. Like I was saying about the salsa class, I mean, I used to go every single Thursday without fail. Rain or shine, even if I had to stay late at the office doing reconciliations, I would still rush over there because it just made me feel so alive and connected to people. And now? I couldn't even tell you the last time I went. My special dancing shoes are just sitting in the back of my closet, probably getting crushed under a pile of old sweaters, and I don't even care. 

And then the painting... I mean, I told you about the water cup being dried out and the brushes just lying there. It’s honestly so jarring to walk past that table. I used to spend hours on a Sunday afternoon just mixing colors, trying to get the exact right shade of blue for the sky in a landscape, and it was so relaxing. It was my time to just decompress from all the numbers and the ledgers. But now, I literally look at those paints and it’s like... nothing. Just a complete blank. It really does feel like I’m looking at the belongings of a stranger, or like a ghost of who I used to be. I don't have even a tiny spark of desire to pick up a brush or try to paint anything. It’s not just that I’m too tired—though I am exhausted—it’s that the actual feeling of wanting to do it, the pleasure I used to get from it, is just completely gone. So, yes, I’d say I’ve pretty much lost interest in all the things that used to make me happy. It's just all gone.
Have you noticed that you feel significantly more tired or have less energy than usual, even when you haven’t been doing anything physically demanding?

Oh, absolutely. It's... it's honestly ridiculous how tired I am. And it's not like a normal tired, you know? Like, back in high school, I used to pull all-nighters studying for finals, and yeah, I'd be exhausted the next day, but a cup of coffee and I'd bounce back. This is totally different. It's like this deep, bone-weary exhaustion that just never goes away. 

Even when I do manage to stay in bed all night—which, like I said, the sleep hasn't been great, but even on the nights where I'm just lying there for eight hours—I'll get up to go to work, and the commute alone wipes me out. I park in this lot that's maybe, I don't know, a block and a half from the accounting firm where I work? It's not far. I used to walk it in heels without even thinking about it. But lately, walking from my car to the front doors... I swear to you, it feels like I'm dragging sandbags tied to my ankles. Every step takes so much effort. By the time I get to my desk and turn on my computer, I feel like I've just run a marathon. 

And then the mental energy... oh my gosh. My job is so detail-oriented. Being a bookkeeping clerk, you have to be sharp. You miss a decimal point or enter a receipt twice, and it throws the whole ledger off. I used to be able to just power through accounts all morning, but now? By lunch, my brain just feels completely worn out. Like it's turned to mush. I'll be staring at a column of numbers, and they just start blurring together, and I have to read the same line item three or four times just to understand what it says. It's so frustrating because I'm just sitting in a chair! I'm not doing manual labor, I'm not lifting heavy boxes, I'm just sitting at a desk typing on a keyboard, and yet I feel completely drained of every ounce of energy I have. So, yeah, the fatigue is just... it's constant, and it's so heavy.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight recently—like eating a lot less or a lot more than usual, or losing or gaining weight without trying?

Yeah, actually, I have. It's funny you ask that because I was just thinking about it the other morning when I was getting dressed for work. I have these black dress pants that I wear to the firm all the time—I bought them maybe six months ago, and they used to fit perfectly, honestly maybe even a little snug around the waist after a big lunch. But when I put them on earlier this week, I had to pull my belt a whole notch tighter. They're just hanging off me. My work pants definitely feel noticeably looser than they did just a few weeks ago, and I haven't been working out or trying to diet or anything like that. 

And it's definitely because my appetite is just completely off. I used to be pretty good about food, you know? I’d try to meal prep on Sundays, make a big batch of pasta or roast some chicken and vegetables so I wouldn't have to stress about it during the week. But lately, the thought of cooking, or even eating a full meal, just seems impossible. Food doesn't even sound good to me anymore. I’ve just been skipping dinner entirely most nights. I get home from the office, and I'm so drained from staring at the ledgers that I just can't bring myself to open the fridge. If I do eat anything, it’s usually just... well, I have this personal budget notebook that I try to update in the evenings, because I like to keep my own finances straight even if work is overwhelming, and I'll just sit there at my kitchen counter and eat plain saltine crackers over it. Literally just munching on dry crackers straight out of the sleeve while I'm looking at my utility bills, because that's all I can stomach. Nothing else sounds appealing, and I just don't have the energy to care about feeding myself a proper meal.
Would you say that your mood has been persistently low or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, rather than just feeling sad occasionally?

Yeah... yeah, it’s definitely not just occasionally. I wish it was just a passing sadness, like when you have a rough day with the accounts or something, but it's not. It’s just... constant. Every single day. Lately, I wake up, and before I even really open my eyes, I already have this... this incredibly heavy, empty feeling. It’s almost like a physical weight pressing down on me. 

And I’ll get out of bed, and I’ll just look around... I mean, I bought this condo a little while ago, and I worked so, so hard for it. I started at the accounting firm right out of high school doing basic data entry and just saved every single penny, skipped going out with friends, worked my way up to bookkeeping clerk just so I could have a place that was entirely mine. I used to be so incredibly proud of it. I used to just walk through the door and feel this huge sense of relief and accomplishment. But now? Lately, just sitting in my own condo, this place that I worked so incredibly hard for, it just makes me want to cry. 

I'll literally just sit on my couch and the tears will start falling, and I can't even explain why. There's just no joy in it anymore. And that feeling, that awful heaviness, it just follows me everywhere. It follows me to the car, it sits with me at my desk while I'm trying to balance the ledgers, and it's right there waiting for me when I come back home. It never really lifts. It’s just this persistent, dark cloud over everything, most of the day, every day. I can't just snap out of it or distract myself with work or TV, because the emptiness is just always there, drowning everything else out. It's like I'm just hollowed out from the inside, all day long.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has experienced a depressed mood most of the day, nearly every day, as part of the diagnostic criteria for major depressive disorder.
doctor.question: Would you say that your mood has been persistently low or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, rather than just feeling sad occasionally?

target_item.name: Depressed_Mood
target_item.manifestation: Lately I wake up with this heavy, empty feeling, like even sitting in my own condo that I worked so hard for just makes me want to cry.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if my mood has been persistently low or depressed most of the day, which directly corresponds to the Depressed Mood symptom.

patient.answer:
Yeah... yeah, it’s definitely not just occasionally. I wish it was just a passing sadness, like when you have a rough day with the accounts or something, but it's not. It’s just... constant. Every single day. Lately, I wake up, and before I even really open my eyes, I already have this... this incredibly heavy, empty feeling. It’s almost like a physical weight pressing down on me. 

And I’ll get out of bed, and I’ll just look around... I mean, I bought this condo a little while ago, and I worked so, so hard for it. I started at the accounting firm right out of high school doing basic data entry and just saved every single penny, skipped going out with friends, worked my way up to bookkeeping clerk just so I could have a place that was entirely mine. I used to be so incredibly proud of it. I used to just walk through the door and feel this huge sense of relief and accomplishment. But now? Lately, just sitting in my own condo, this place that I worked so incredibly hard for, it just makes me want to cry. 

I'll literally just sit on my couch and the tears will start falling, and I can't even explain why. There's just no joy in it anymore. And that feeling, that awful heaviness, it just follows me everywhere. It follows me to the car, it sits with me at my desk while I'm trying to balance the ledgers, and it's right there waiting for me when I come back home. It never really lifts. It’s just this persistent, dark cloud over everything, most of the day, every day. I can't just snap out of it or distract myself with work or TV, because the emptiness is just always there, drowning everything else out. It's like I'm just hollowed out from the inside, all day long.

inference.note: The patient meets criteria for major depressive disorder, moderate (F32.1) based on persistent depressed mood, loss of interest/pleasure (anhedonia), significant fatigue, decreased appetite/weight loss, and impaired function nearly every day for at least 2 weeks. No features of anxiety disorders (F51.0, F51.2) were confirmed.
